body:
`get_locale()` (cps/cw_babel.py:53-56) returns `current_user.locale` verbatim for
any logged-in non-Guest user. The value is not constrained to the locales we ship.

Validation on the write side is inconsistent:

- `cps/admin.py:947` DOES validate: `if vals['value'] in get_available_translations()`.
- `cps/web.py:2908` does NOT: `current_user.locale = to_save.get("locale", "en")`.
  This is the self-service profile route, so any authenticated user can store an
  arbitrary string as their own locale.
- `cps/admin.py:2888` and `cps/admin.py:3148` also assign without validation.

The `?lang=` per-request override IS validated (`_coerce_locale` against
available), so the stored-locale path is the gap.

Impact found so far: the value flowed into a filesystem path segment in
`render_template.translations_missing_notification`, where `'../../..'` resolved
to `cps/LC_MESSAGES` — outside the translations tree. Fixed at that callsite in
PR #1449 with a containment assertion, but the callsite is the symptom. Other
consumers of `get_locale()` inherit the same untrusted value, and each one has to
remember to defend itself.

The root fix is to validate on write in `web.py:2908` (and the two admin
assignments) against `get_available_translations()`, matching what
`admin.py:947` already does, so `get_locale()` can be trusted by its callers.

Authenticated-only and low reach on its own; filed rather than shipped because
the write-side fix touches three routes and wants its own change.

Not user-reported. Surfaced while fixing #1447.
title: user.locale is stored unvalidated and reaches get_locale() verbatim
